drawings.description: Les trois graphes de (65) sont dessinés : un cercle portant un sommet marqué « 1 » ; deux sommets marqués « 1 » reliés par deux arcs ; un cercle avec une queue dont le bout est marqué « 2 ». En regard, les courbes correspondantes : une courbe nodale (en huit) portant un point $a$ ; deux droites se coupant en deux points, portant $a$ et $b$ ; une courbe nodale à laquelle est attachée une droite portant $a$ et $b$.
drawings.kind: MD graphs of (65) and the corresponding stable curves
drawings.notes: Left: the three graphs of (65): a loop on a vertex of weight 1; two vertices of weight 1 joined by two arcs; a loop with a tail whose end has weight 2. Right: the corresponding curves: a nodal curve (figure eight) with a; two lines meeting in two points, with a and b; a nodal curve with a line attached carrying a and b. Encoded twice, the graphs (weights as legs) and the dual graphs of the curves: the two encodings coincide and give types (1,1), (1,2), (1,2) with ambient dimension 3g - 3 + nu = nu = 1, 2, 2, as in (65). The legends nu = ... = dim amb G are text. The labels a, b on the curves are small; the a of the first curve is not clearly visible.

Encoded as stable graphs: all five are of type (1,2), and their stratum dimensions 2, 1, 1, 0, 0 match the column codimensions 0, 1, 1, 2, 2. The arrows (specialisations) are not encoded.

drawings.description: schéma raturé : un graphe à deux sommets marqués $I' \setminus \{a'\}$ et $I''$, entouré d'un contour en forme de cloche ; en dessous, un segment dont l'extrémité gauche porte un symbole surchargé
drawings.kind: struck schema: graph in a bell-shaped contour
drawings.notes: Redrawn on a tight crop. The contour as one course: down the left side, round the bottom of the left lobe, up the straight flank to the peak, down the right side to the bottom of the right lobe; from there a straight stroke rises to the upper right and turns down and out to the right; a second stroke falls from the upper right to the lower right corner, where the long bottom line starts (the corner computed once); the two strokes cross at the upper right. The horizontal stroke at the level of the text line ends on the flank (computed point). Below, the segment with a point at each end; I' \ {a'} and I'' inside the lobes. Left out: the overinked symbol under the left end of the segment, the text line at the top and the words at the left of the horizontal stroke. The transcription calls the schema struck (raturé); no stroke can be told apart as the strike (the crossing strokes at the upper right, drawn grey before, continue the contour), so the whole is drawn in ink: to check. The two vertices of the graph are not marked on the page; the labels stand where he wrote them. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.kind: graph with flattened loops
drawings.notes: Graph: a vertex with two short free segments ("boucles aplaties") is joined to a second vertex; this one is joined to a third by two parallel edges (one straight, one curved), the third to a fourth that carries a loop; a vertex below, joined to the second, carries three free segments. Drawn as on the page. The transcription calls the vertex with two flattened loops "de degre trois" and joins it directly by the two parallel edges; on the page the two flattened loops end at a separate dot joined to the vertex that carries the parallel edges (the dots may mark the ends of the flattened loops). Not encoded: whether the dots are vertices or loop ends is not fixed by the figure alone.
